answer: In a Wesolowski VDF, each identity’s challenge requires a prescribed chain of modular squarings, where every step depends on the previous one. GPUs can run separate chains for separate clones, but cannot shortcut one chain through parallelism; each clone therefore incurs a real sequential delay, limiting how quickly identities can be produced. Quartz, velvet, and opal may label instances, but do not change this physical time bottleneck.
